title: Edge-prefetch serialization mismatch caused early-EOS in regional rollout - notes and action items
summary: During a staged variant rollout that enabled edge-prefetch and advanced KV serialization in eu-west, a subset of long-context requests were terminated early with EOS tokens. This manifested as customer-facing truncation for prompts > 8k tokens and increased error rates for streaming sessions. The issue was detected by synthetic canaries and reported by two enterprise customers in the EU region.
impact: Users in eu-west experienced truncated outputs and dropped streaming sessions. Affected customers: 2 enterprise tenants (chatbot and document-summarization pipelines). Estimated error budget burn for the day: 12%. No data leak or model corruption observed. Median p95 generation latency increased due to retries for affected requests.
detection:
10:15 UTC - eu-west synthetic canaries showed 8% EOS spike on long-context suite.
10:22 UTC - Customer alerts from tenant-A and tenant-B reporting truncated responses.
10:30 UTC - SRE oncall started investigation, correlated canaries to customer traces.
10:45 UTC - Observed region-specific increase in 'eos_emitted_early' metric across edge nodes running variant v2-prefetch.
11:05 UTC - Reproduced locally by replaying a captured request against v2-prefetch in eu-west staging; confirmed early-EOS when KV cache hit path serialized from nodes running old runtime ABI.
timeline:
2024-10-28 09:50 UTC - Rollout of model variant v2-prefetch started (regional rollout: eu-west first).
2024-10-28 10:15 UTC - First canary deviations noticed.
2024-10-28 10:22 UTC - Customer reports.
2024-10-28 10:45 UTC - Metric correlation and node grouping identified: only nodes with feature_flag=edge-prefetch=true and runtime image runtime:1.18.0 showed the problem.
2024-10-28 10:50 UTC - Scoped to kv-serialization module after decoding traces showed mismatched header size.
2024-10-28 11:15 UTC - Emergency rollback of v2-prefetch in eu-west region started.
2024-10-28 11:40 UTC - Rollback completed; canaries returned to baseline by 11:55 UTC.
2024-10-28 12:30 UTC - Post-rollback verification and postmortem kickoff meeting scheduled.
mitigation_steps:
1) Immediately disabled edge-prefetch feature flag in eu-west and initiated rollback of model variant v2-prefetch.
2) Quarantined nodes that had received a mixed set of runtime binaries (some nodes had a back-compat shim missing).
3) Applied temporary traffic routing to fallback cluster (dedicated-hosted pathway) for impacted tenants.
4) Increased canary sampling for long-context suites across all regions until fix validated.
5) Notified customer success and sent a status update to affected tenants.
root_cause: A subtle serialization format mismatch in the KV prefetch path. The new prefetch code introduced a compact header (version 2) that assumes a 64-bit little-endian layout for timestamp and length fields. A subset of eu-west edge machines were still running an older runtime binary with an ABI shim that expected the previous header (version 1) and performed sign-extension on a 32-bit length field. When a v2-prefetched KV packet produced by a correctly built process arrived at a process with the older ABI, the decoder misread the length and treated padding as an end-of-sequence marker, causing an immediate EOS emission. Contributing factor: a regional config drift where the feature flag rollout gate for 'edge-prefetch' flipped on at the CDN layer but the runtime image rollout was staggered and not strictly pinned, creating mixed-version interop during traffic handover.
what_went_well:
- Canary tests caught the regression quickly and provided a reproducible signal.
- Rollback tooling for variant swaps worked and brought canaries back to baseline within ~45 minutes.
- Clear oncall communication channels (escalation, SRE, SE customer reps) reduced customer noise and provided timely updates.
what_failed:
- Lack of schema/version negotiation for KV serialization allowed silent incompatibility.
- Rollout gating did not enforce image+feature-flag atomicity; feature flags could flip before runtime images were consistent.
- Insufficient integration tests for mixed-version interop on the prefetch/kv path (no simulated old-ABI consumer with new-ABI producer in staging).
- Region-specific rollout plan did not include an explicit cross-check for binary version parity at service handshake time.
permanent_fix_proposal:
1) Add explicit serialization header with a magic number and schema version; decoder rejects unknown versions and logs a high-severity metric.
2) Enforce atomic rollout constraint in orchestration: feature-flag activation for a region must be gated on runtime image parity (image tag check).
3) Add mixed-version interop tests to CI that simulate new-prefetch -> old-decoder and old-prefetch -> new-decoder.
4) Expand canary suites to include long-context streaming scenarios and add an 'eos_emitted_early' synthetic assertion.
5) Add a post-deploy probe that verifies handshake schema compatibility across all edge nodes in a region before increasing traffic.
action_items:
- PR #3241: serialization header + versioning (assign: Samir, due: 2024-11-08).
- Orchestrator change: atomic rollout gating (assign: Marta, due: 2024-11-12).
- CI job: mixed-version interop matrix (assign: Ethan, due: 2024-11-05).
- Run a regional audit of image tags vs feature flags and produce a one-time reconciliation script (assign: Priya, due: 2024-11-04).
- Customer follow-up: CS to schedule post-incident review with affected tenants and share remediation plan (assign: Lina Chen, due: 2024-11-06).
follow_up_notes:
- Replayed 10 representative failing requests and validated they succeed after applying serialization header check in local staging.
- No evidence of model parameter corruption; weights were unchanged.
- Consider adding a runtime-messaging contract test at the binary handshake layer.
- We should discuss whether to add automated rollback thresholds based on 'eos_emitted_early' metric to reduce MTTD/MTTR for similar future regressions.

extra_notes: This incident highlights the risk of rolling out protocol changes that are not backward compatible (even if compact). Going forward we should treat any serialization or wire-format change as a major compatibility event and require explicit opt-in and multi-stage validation. Also consider enhancing our observability to detect header/parsing errors earlier (decoder-level counters and decode-failure traces).
